listing.promotionalText: Ask a Bible question and see the passages behind the answer, or flip through 179 flashcards. Free, no sign-in. Answers can contain mistakes, so check the verses.
listing.description:
Shalom is a free Bible study companion for iPhone and iPad. Ask a question in plain language, read an answer with the Scripture passages it draws on, and learn with flashcards.

ASK SHALOM
Type a question about a passage, a theme or a hard topic. Shalom looks up verses in the Berean Standard Bible and writes an answer that points to them. Tap a reference to open the full passage. Each reference is marked as looked up before answering or not checked, so you can inspect the passages yourself.

AI answers can be wrong or incomplete. Shalom is a study aid, not a pastor, a counselor or a replacement for reading Scripture yourself. Please read the passages and check anything that matters to you.

FLASHCARDS
Browse 179 flashcards in two sets: 50 quick facts and 129 discover questions with teaching notes. Tap Show answer, read the explanation and move to the next card. Cards work offline, and you can send any card to chat to explore it further.

FREE, WITHOUT AN ACCOUNT
Every feature is free. There are no subscriptions, purchases or ads, and you do not need to sign in. Your conversations are kept in a private cache on your device.

PRIVACY
To write an answer, your question and recent conversation turns are sent over the internet to Shalom's server and to the AI model service it uses. Please do not include personal information in your questions.

MADE FOR READING
A calm, quiet layout with a sidebar on iPad and a slide-out drawer on iPhone. Verse text is from the Berean Standard Bible, which is in the public domain.

review.notes:
LOCAL APP STORE TEMPLATE, review before use; not entered as public App Store review notes.

Review instructions for Shalom 0.1.3 (4):

Shalom opens as a guest. Every feature is free; native sign-in and all purchasing are disabled. No account or demo credentials are needed.

1. Enter a question such as "What does John 3:16 mean?" and tap Send. The first attempt opens an AI-sharing disclosure before transmission. Not Now keeps sharing off. Allow AI Answers records permission but does not send: tap Send again deliberately to receive an answer. The disclosure names Shalom, OpenRouter and the routed AI provider, recent-chat context and retention/training uncertainty.
2. Open Sources below the answer. Each reference is marked looked up before answering or not checked. Tap a reference to read its Bible passage. Answers may contain mistakes; a checked reference is not a guarantee of a correct interpretation.
3. Open the sidebar/drawer, then Account > Privacy. The app has offline privacy facts, a published policy at https://sholam.vercel.app/privacy and support at https://sholam.vercel.app/support. Account can revoke AI sharing or confirm deletion of local guest chats. Deletion cannot recall provider/server copies.
4. Open Flashcards from the drawer on iPhone or the Chat / Flashcards switch on iPad. The 179 canonical cards are bundled for offline reading. Show answer, Next and Ask Shalom are explicit actions; asking still follows the permission gate.
5. Report below a completed answer prepares a draft with answer text excluded by default. Inclusion is opt-in. Copy is local with expiry; Share opens the system recipient chooser. There is no automatic report upload or receipt claim.

The native Release configuration was checked on a simulator against the live service, including a completed answer and both published links. This is not a claim of physical-device TestFlight installation. Free-model availability and service usage limits can affect response times.
